script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

Title: THE MUG AND THE MOON

INT. CAFE - DAY

A cozy indie café, filled with the aroma of freshly brewed coffee and the gentle hum of conversation. The walls are adorned with quirky art. At the corner table, two FRIENDS, JANE (mid-30s, artistic, introverted) and MARK (early 30s, goofy, extroverted), sit facing each other.

JANE
(sighs, looking at her half-finished painting)
I can't seem to get this right.

MARK
(smiling)
Hey, you've almost finished it. Just a few more touches. And I have an idea!

JANE
(raising an eyebrow)
What's your idea?

MARK
(grinning)
Let's take a walk around the block. Maybe some fresh air will inspire you.

They finish their drinks and head out into the sunny day.

INT. PARK - DAY

Jane and Mark stroll through the park, admiring the flowers and the birds. They discuss their art and their lives, laughing and joking.

JANE
(looking at Mark)
You know, I've never seen you take this seriously before.

MARK
(laughs)
Well, when it comes to you and your art, I'll always be serious.

They share a warm smile.

INT. ART SUPPLY STORE - DAY

Jane and Mark browse the shelves of the art supply store, looking for inspiration. They find a new brand of paints and canvas, and Jane is immediately drawn to them.

MARK
See, this is why I brought you here. You deserve the best.

JANE
(smiling)
Thank you, Mark.

INT. CAFE - NIGHT

Jane and Mark return to the café, where they set up their easels and begin working on their paintings. The café's owner, LUCY (late 30s, kind, observant), looks on approvingly.

LUCY
(smiling)
It's so nice to see you both so passionate about your art.

MARK
(grinning)
Thanks, Lucy. We're really enjoying ourselves.

INT. CAFE - NIGHT (LATER)

The café begins to empty out as the evening wears on. Jane and Mark pack up their things, satisfied with their progress.

JANE
(looking at Mark)
We make a good team.

MARK
(laughs)
You have no idea.

They share a heartfelt hug, knowing that their friendship is the foundation of their creativity.

FADE OUT.

THE END
